renewal_failure_transition: If replacement creation fails by expiry, transition status to blocked_expired and record the failure in blockers; do not continue cycles under the expired job.
last_cycle_summary: Cycle 10 delivered the M1 run-stdin slice through PR #17, squash-merged as 67d39f2 with both required CI runs green on both commits. start_process now pipes child stdin (previously the child inherited the backend's own stdin); new v1 requests send_input/close_stdin deliver input to running runs with accepted/not_found/closed statuses, and Swift IPCClient mirrors them. Accepted means delivered modulo racing exit: pre-spawn input is buffered and flushed at publication. Implemented by a Codex gpt-5.6-sol worker; the orchestrator caught a register-to-publish data-loss race the worker's sandbox could not test (its cat test failed deterministically) and a second sol worker added the buffering state machine. Independent Codex sol review then found 2 blockers/2 majors, all confirmed: blocking pipe writes under the per-run mutex could wedge all 8 IPC slots including cancel, and a synchronous pre-publication flush could block the supervision thread past timeout/cancel; accepted was returned for knowably undeliverable input; close was not a stable boundary. A third sol worker redesigned delivery: senders only enqueue, the run supervision thread drains to a non-blocking fd each tick, input_response gained status closed, and close is a stable boundary that still delivers buffered bytes before EOF. Runtime demo: echo 0.03s, post-close send returns closed, 700 KiB enqueued on a paused run in 0.35s with cancel accepted 0.00s later. Known flagged limitation: the per-run stdin queue is unbounded. M1 remains active for PTYs, waiting-input detection, redaction/metadata, durable state, budget expiry, and temporary/worktree cleanup.
